title: Build the conditional flow matching loss
goal:
Implement the optimal-transport (OT) conditional flow matching loss from Section 4.1. Write two functions.

`ot_pair(x0, x1, t, sigma_min)` takes noise `x0` and data `x1`, both of shape `(n, d)`, and times `t` of shape `(n,)`. It returns `(xt, ut)`: the point on the conditional flow, $\psi_t(x_0) = (1 - (1 - \sigma_{\min})\,t)\,x_0 + t\,x_1$ (Equation 22), and its regression target $x_1 - (1 - \sigma_{\min})\,x_0$ (Equation 23).

`cfm_loss(v, x0, x1, t, sigma_min)` returns the Monte Carlo estimate of $\mathcal{L}_{\text{CFM}}$ (Equation 23): the mean over the batch of the squared Euclidean norm $\lVert v_t(x_t) - u_t \rVert^2$. Here `v(x, t)` takes `x` of shape `(n, d)` and `t` of shape `(n,)` and returns shape `(n, d)`.

The page's example: with $\sigma_{\min} = 0.1$, $x_0 = -1$, $x_1 = 2$, and $t = 0.5$, the point is $x_t = 0.45$ and the target is $2.9$.
hints: `t` has shape `(n,)`. Use `t[:, None]` so it broadcasts against the `(n, d)` arrays.
The target doesn't depend on `t`. It is a constant velocity for each pair, which is why the OT path is a straight line.
Square the difference, sum over the last axis (the $d$ coordinates), then average over the batch. Averaging over every entry instead divides by $d$ and gives the wrong value.
At $t = 0$ the point is $x_0$. At $t = 1$ it is $x_1 + \sigma_{\min} x_0$, so the target equals the displacement over one unit of time.
